case_name: The Durgah Committee, Ajmer Andanother v Syed Hussain Ali And Others
facts: In the High Court of Judicature for Rajasthan at Jodhpur a writ petition was filed under Art. 226 of the Constitution by the nine respondents who are Khadims of the tomb of Khwaja Moinud-din Chishti of Ajmer challenging the vires of the Durgah Khwaja Saheb Act XXXVI of 1955.
The shrine of Nazrat Khwaja Moin-ud-din Chishti which is generally known as the Durgah Khwaja Saheb situated at Ajmer is one of the most important places of pilgrimage for the muslims of India.
Khwaja Saheb came to India sometime towards the end of the 12th Century A.D. and settled down in Ajmer.
The respondents' case further is that after his death the tomb under which the saint was interred was a kutcha structure and continued to be such for nearly 300 years thereafter.
Khwaja Syed Fukhuruddin and Sheikh Mohammad Yadgar, who originally accompanied the Khwaja Saheb Syed to India, were his close and devoted followers.
issues: The vires of the Durgah Khwaja Saheb Act XXXVI of 1955
The rights of the Khadims to manage the shrine and receive offerings
petitioner_arguments: The respondents alleged that the Act in general and the provisions specified in the petition in particular are ultra vires
They claimed a direction or an appropriate writ or order restraining the appellants from enforcing any of its provisions
Their fundamental rights to property and their fundamental right to manage the said property were being taken away
respondent_arguments: The appellants averred that the circle of devotees of, and visitors to, the shrine was not confined to the Chishtia Order; but it included devotees and pilgrims of all classes of people following different religions
They denied that the Durgah was looked after by the descendants of Syed Fukhuruddin and Mohamad Yadgar
Their case was that the Khadims were and are no more, than servants of the holy tomb and their duties are similar to those of chowkidars
court_reasoning: The High Court has found that the offerings made before the tomb for nearly 400 years before the tomb was rebuilt into a pucca structure must have been used by the Khadims for themselves

It also held that the Khadims were performing several duties set out by the respondents and that it was mainly the Khadims who circulated the stories of miracles performed by Khwaja Saheb during his lifetime

The High Court has found that s. 2(b)(v) violates Art. 19(1)(f), s. 5 violates Art. 26, s. 11(f) Arts. 19(1)(g) and 25(1), ss. 11(b) and 13(1) Art. 25, s. 14 Art. 19(1)(f) and as. 16 and 18 Art. 14 read with Art. 32
holding: The High Court has made a declaration that the impugned provisions of the Act are ultra vires and has issued an order restraining the appellants from enforcing them
The whole of the Act has in substance been rendered inoperative
